# Engine trouble codes (VQ40DE)

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Connect an OBD-II reader and turn the ignition on. [t12]

Inspect the passenger side plug color to determine fuel mixture and identify potential leaks. [t343]

Check for a P011 code indicating timing issues. [t101]

[Partial] Check grounds near the battery, inspect the ground connection underneath the air box, monitor Long Term Fuel Trims, then check voltages. [t132]

[Partial] Look for trouble code P1283, noting it indicates a Bank 2 lean condition and checking fuel pressure. [t132]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

2. Turn the ignition key to the ON position without starting the engine.

2. Inspect the passenger side (Bank 1) plug color to determine fuel mixture.

## Tips & gotchas

- Look out for symptoms like 'rumble strip' vibrations between 45 and 60 mph before full transmission failure. [t24]
- Symptoms often progress from hard shifts to complete slipping within about 2,000 miles. [t24]
- Look for a bright white appearance on Bank 1 plugs, which indicates a lean condition. [t343]
- If the passenger side plugs are dark brown instead of white, suspect a leak after the combustion chamber causing the ECM to over-fuel that bank. [t343]
- Monitor Long Term Fuel Trims (LTFT) to see if they are excessively lean before swapping parts. [t132]
- Check voltages at the sensor and ECU after verifying grounds. [t132]
- Note that this code points to a lean condition on Bank 2. [t132]
- Check fuel pressure as another potential variable. [t132]
